components.description: Unpaid job-protected pregnancy leave of up to 17 weeks for a birth mother with 13 weeks of service, a leave from all duties; SPS C4 restates ESA ss. 46-47 without adding length, so it is coded as the statute.
components.faculty_group_note: faculty and MUFA senior academic librarians (SPS C4 footnote 1); 'Full-time and regular part-time McMaster faculty members and MUFA librarians'
components.entitlement_note: Statutory leave (ESA s. 46: 'is entitled'); SPS C4 II ii: 'may request and will be granted'.
components.duration_note: ESA s. 47(1)(a): ends 17 weeks after it began; s. 47(2) and SPS C4 III let the employee end it earlier ('electing not to take the maximum amount of time available'). SPS C4 IV: mothers of children needing lengthy post-natal hospital care may delay all or part of the leave until the child is released.
components.service_requirement: 13 weeks continuous employment before the estimated date of delivery (SPS C4 II ii; ESA s. 46(1): due date not fewer than 13 weeks after employment began)
components.notice: as much notice as possible, normally at least two weeks (SPS C4 III); ESA s. 46(4) written notice two weeks before
components.time_window: begins no sooner than 17 weeks before the anticipated delivery date and no later than the date of birth
components.relief_note: SPS C4 II ii: relieved of all duties including teaching, graduate supervision, research and service.

faculty_group: This policy applies to faculty and to those senior academic librarians who are members of the McMaster University Faculty Association (MUFA).

Full-time and regular part-time McMaster faculty members and MUFA librarians, who have at least thirteen (13) weeks continuous employment at the University prior to the estimated date of delivery or adoption of a child (or children), may request and will be granted a pregnancy and/or parental leave.
eligible_parent: Only birth mothers are able to take pregnancy leave whereas all parents, as defined above, are eligible for parental leave.
entitlement: A pregnant employee is entitled to a leave of absence without pay unless her due date falls fewer than 13 weeks after she commenced employment.

Full-time and regular part-time McMaster faculty members and MUFA librarians, who have at least thirteen (13) weeks continuous employment at the University prior to the estimated date of delivery or adoption of a child (or children), may request and will be granted a pregnancy and/or parental leave.
duration: An employee’s pregnancy leave ends, (a) if she is entitled to parental leave, 17 weeks after the pregnancy leave began;
An employee may end her leave earlier than the day set out in subsection (1) by giving her employer written notice at least four weeks before the day she wishes to end her leave.
Pregnancy leave begins no later than the date of the birth of the child (or children) and no sooner than 17 weeks prior to the anticipated delivery date.
A faculty member or MUFA librarian electing not to take the maximum amount of time available for a leave will not have the option of taking any untaken leave at a later date.
service_requirement: who have at least thirteen (13) weeks continuous employment at the University prior to the estimated date of delivery or adoption of a child (or children)
A pregnant employee is entitled to a leave of absence without pay unless her due date falls fewer than 13 weeks after she commenced employment.
relief: Pregnancy and parental leaves are leaves of absence during which a faculty member or MUFA librarian is relieved of all duties including teaching, graduate supervision, research and service.
statute_source: specifically the provincial Employment Standards Act, 2000 (“ESA”) and the federal Employment Insurance Act (“EIA”)

components.description: Unpaid job-protected parental leave for all parents (birth, non-birth, adoptive), a leave from all duties. SPS C4 (2011 text) states 35 weeks after pregnancy leave and 37 otherwise, the pre-December-2017 statute; it adds no length to the statute, so it is coded as ESA ss. 48-49 in force on the reference date: 61 weeks after a pregnancy leave, 63 otherwise.
components.faculty_group_note: faculty and MUFA senior academic librarians (SPS C4 footnote 1)
components.eligible_parent_wording: all parents, as defined above (birth parents; a person with whom a child is placed for adoption; a person in a relationship of some permanence with the parent who intends to treat the child as his or her own; same-sex parents)
components.entitlement_note: Statutory leave (ESA s. 48: 'is entitled'); SPS C4 V: 'is entitled to unpaid parental leave'.
components.duration_note: ESA s. 49(1) in force on 2018-02-24 (amended 2017-12-03): 61 weeks if the employee also took pregnancy leave, 63 otherwise; s. 49(2) lets the employee end it earlier. Coded from the statute (U2).

components.time_window: SPS C4 (2011): must begin no later than 52 weeks after the birth or placement; ESA s. 48(2) in force on the reference date: no later than 78 weeks

components.relief_note: SPS C4 II ii: relieved of all duties including teaching, graduate supervision, research and service.

sequence.note: For a birth mother, parental leave commences when her pregnancy leave ends (SPS C4 V; ESA s. 48(3)). The non-birth parent starts it at the birth.

faculty_group: This policy applies to faculty and to those senior academic librarians who are members of the McMaster University Faculty Association (MUFA).

Full-time and regular part-time McMaster faculty members and MUFA librarians, who have at least thirteen (13) weeks continuous employment at the University prior to the estimated date of delivery or adoption of a child (or children), may request and will be granted a pregnancy and/or parental leave.
eligible_parent: Only birth mothers are able to take pregnancy leave whereas all parents, as defined above, are eligible for parental leave.

the Employment Standards Act (ESA) defines a parent as including “a person with whom a child is placed for adoption and a person who is in a relationship of some permanence with the parent of the child and who intends to treat the child as his or her own.”
entitlement: An employee who has been employed by his or her employer for at least 13 weeks and who is the parent of a child is entitled to a leave of absence without pay following the birth of the child or the coming of the child into the employee’s custody, care and control for the first time.

An employee taking a pregnancy leave is entitled to unpaid parental leave of 35 weeks in addition to the paid weeks of pregnancy leave. For a birth mother, parental leave commences when her pregnancy leave ends.
duration: An employee’s parental leave ends 61 weeks after it began, if the employee also took pregnancy leave and 63 weeks after it began, otherwise.

A faculty member or MUFA librarian electing not to take the maximum amount of time available for a leave will not have the option of taking any untaken leave at a later date.

An employee taking a pregnancy leave is entitled to unpaid parental leave of 35 weeks in addition to the paid weeks of pregnancy leave. For a birth mother, parental leave commences when her pregnancy leave ends.
An employee who has not taken a pregnancy leave prior to her parental leave is entitled to 37 weeks of unpaid parental leave (the two week qualifying period under the EIA plus 35 weeks).
duration_by_role: An employee’s parental leave ends 61 weeks after it began, if the employee also took pregnancy leave and 63 weeks after it began, otherwise.
A faculty member or MUFA librarian electing not to take the maximum amount of time available for a leave will not have the option of taking any untaken leave at a later date.
service_requirement: who have at least thirteen (13) weeks continuous employment at the University prior to the estimated date of delivery or adoption of a child (or children)

An employee who has been employed by his or her employer for at least 13 weeks and who is the parent of a child is entitled to a leave of absence without pay following the birth of the child or the coming of the child into the employee’s custody, care and control for the first time.
relief: Pregnancy and parental leaves are leaves of absence during which a faculty member or MUFA librarian is relieved of all duties including teaching, graduate supervision, research and service.
sequence: An employee taking a pregnancy leave is entitled to unpaid parental leave of 35 weeks in addition to the paid weeks of pregnancy leave. For a birth mother, parental leave commences when her pregnancy leave ends.
An employee who has taken pregnancy leave must begin her parental leave when her pregnancy leave ends unless the child has not yet come into her custody, care and control for the first time.
dual_employee_rule: Both parents are eligible to take a parental leave provided that the total period of their combined leaves does not exceed 35 or 37 weeks, as the case may be.
time_window: A parental leave must begin no later than 52 weeks after the birth of the child or, in the case of adoption of a child, after the child first comes into the custody, care and control of the parent.

notes: 2018_00_link.txt is SPS C4 Pregnancy/Parental Leave Policy for Faculty and MUFA Librarians, December 2011 version, Wayback 2015-04-17; 2018_01_jc_remuneration_agreement_2017_2019.txt is the transcribed Joint Committee Remuneration Agreement 2017-2019; 2018_02_mufa_remuneration_chair_report_mar2017.txt is a MUFA memo, March 17, 2017 (explanatory); 2018_03_tenure_promotion_policy_rev_june2017.txt is the Tenure and Promotion Policy, 2019 compilation.

Governing documents: SPS C4 is the faculty pregnancy/parental leave policy, so missing is false (the no-policy coding (`missing`)). Its saved copy is the December 2011 version; the Tenure and Promotion Policy cover lists revisions to SPS C4 on July 1, 2015 and June 7, 2017, and the Joint Committee Agreement revises its 'Section V (i) Financial Benefits' (numbering not in the 2011 copy, where financial benefits are II iii), so the version in force on 2018-02-24 is not saved: components resting on the 2011 text are flagged version_uncertain and cross_reference_not_saved.

Financial benefits in force on the reference date: the Joint Committee Remuneration Agreement (signed March 13, 2017, effective July 1, 2017) replaces SPS C4's financial-benefit options. Coded: Option A (pregnancy top-up 11 weeks + parental top-up 19 weeks at 95% less the EI Max; c6, c7) or Option B (100% salary for the first four weeks of either leave; c8), at the member's election. The superseded December 2011 options are not coded as components: Option A, 100% for weeks 1-2 then 90% less the EI Max to week 19; Option B, four weeks with full salary within the first 26 weeks; and 'A birth mother who does not opt to receive financial benefits during her pregnancy leave may choose between one of the two options available for financial benefits during parental leave.' The MUFA memo confirms the earlier top-up covered 'either a 19 week pregnancy leave or a 19 week parental leave, but not both'.

Eligibility for the University's financial benefits (2011 text): 13 weeks of continuous service and enrolment in the Salary Continuance/LTD program; members in a period of notice (resignation, dismissal, non-renewal) receive no University benefits for any period beyond the termination date; benefits only within 52 weeks of birth or placement.

Parental leave length: the saved SPS C4 states 35 weeks after a pregnancy leave and 37 otherwise (the ESA before 2017-12-03, now s. 49(1.1) for children born before that date). On 2018-02-24 ESA s. 49(1) gives 61 and 63 weeks, and s. 48(2) lets the leave start up to 78 weeks after the birth (SPS C4: 52). c2 is coded from the statute and flagged.

Benefits during leave (SPS C4 II iv, 2011): no loss in salary level; pension, health, disability and other benefits continue if the member pays the normal share; vacation and research leave continue to accrue. II v: where a pregnancy or parental leave overlaps another approved leave, the other leave's salary provisions continue and the non-overlapping portion receives Option A or B; vacation falling in the leave may be taken in the twelve months after; an overlapping research leave's unused portion normally follows the leave. These are not separate components.

Not components: the Child Care Allowance (Joint Committee Agreement s. 5: up to $2,500 per dependant under 7 per year, from a $500,000 pool, effective July 1, 2017; MUFA memo) is an annual cash allowance, not leave, pay during leave, relief or protection. SPS C4 IV's option to delay pregnancy leave while a newborn is hospitalised is recorded in c1's duration_note.

Documents cited but not saved: SPS C4 as revised July 1, 2015 and June 7, 2017; SPS C1 and C2 Research Leave Policies; SPS C3 Unpaid Leaves of Absence; SPS C5 Faculty Reduced Workload Policy; SPS C6 Faculty Reduced Workload Policy - Phase-in to Retirement; the University's Policy on Workplace Accommodation; the Salary Continuance/LTD program terms; Appendix B 'Reduced Workload Provisions'. Pension Plan Section 7.04 (cited in the Joint Committee Agreement) is unrelated to leave.

Tenure and Promotion Policy version: the file is a 2019 compilation (cover lists revisions through June 19, 2019); clause II.7 (tenure-clock extensions) was last revised July 1, 2015, so c11, c12 and c14 are in force on 2018-02-24. The Policy states that it takes precedence over any SPS, so its automatic one-year extension (c11) governs over the 2011 SPS C4 VII opt-in deferral (c13, flagged conflicting_sources).

Population: the Joint Committee Agreement covers 'faculty members who participate in the Career Progress/Merit Scheme and MUFA Librarians'; SPS C4 covers faculty and MUFA senior academic librarians, full-time and regular part-time. MUFA is a non-certified association; the Agreement is its negotiated settlement with the Administration.

Birth parent chain: pregnancy leave 17 (c1; Option A pregnancy top-up c6 within it, weeks 1-11; EI maternity c4 from week 2, 15 weeks) -> parental leave 61 (c2; Option A parental top-up c7 within it, its first 19 weeks; EI parental c5 consecutive_after EI maternity, 35 weeks). Alternative: Option B c8, the first 4 weeks of the pregnancy leave at 100%, in_lieu_of c6 and c7. The discretionary pregnancy-leave extension c3 (no length) follows c1.

Non-birth parent chain: parental leave 63 (c2, from the birth; Option A parental top-up c7 within it, 19 weeks; EI parental c5 concurrent_with c2 from week 2, 35 weeks). Alternative: Option B c8, the first 4 weeks of the parental leave at 100%, in_lieu_of c7.
No calendar: no document states a term length or kind of term.
